cards.text: Last chapter, Wisdom stood out in the street YELLING for anybody who'd listen (Prov 1:20). Now a father sits his son down and opens with one little word: IF. Friend, he is about to stack up conditions like cookie trays on a cooling rack.

cards.question: The father's very first IF is about his own words. What does he hope his son will do with them?

cards.text: He adds hide my commandments within you, and the IFs keep stacking up: turn your ear to wisdom, point your heart at understanding. This man writes instructions like a recipe card, and he is NOT on the last step yet.

cards.question: When it comes to insight, the son is told to truly call out to it. He's told to lift his ___ to understanding.

cards.text: Then the father tells his son just how hard to look for wisdom. Not a casual look, friend, this is flipping every couch cushion for your car keys when you are ALREADY LATE.

cards.question: The father paints a picture of how hard to look for wisdom. He says to search for it the way people search for what?

answers.text: A lost coin and a lost sheep

cards.question: All those IFs lead to one big THEN. If the son seeks wisdom like treasure, what does he discover?

cards.text: Now here's the twist. The son does all that digging, but he doesn't make the treasure. He just brings the shovel.

cards.question: The son does the searching, but the ___ is the one who gives wisdom.

cards.text: The LORD stores up sound wisdom for the upright, like a cookie box set aside with your name on it. And friend, He's got one more title on His business card.

cards.question: To those who walk with integrity, the LORD is a ___.
The LORD guards the paths of justice and protects the way of His saints.

cards.text: And here comes ANOTHER then. Then you will discern, he says, the same four words he used back in verse 5, because this dad does not waste a good line.

cards.question: This time the father says the son will discern every good path. Which ones does he name?

cards.text: Wisdom doesn't just knock on the door, friend. It walks right into the son's heart, unpacks its bags and puts its toothbrush by the sink.

cards.question: Once wisdom enters the son's heart, knowledge will feel like a heavy load on his soul.
With wisdom moved into the son's heart, what will watch over him and guard him?

cards.text: Discretion and understanding aren't standing guard for decoration, friend. They're there to deliver the son from the way of evil and from the man who speaks perversity.

These folks leave the straight paths to walk in the ways of darkness. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a dark junk drawer waiting for the light, and these people are walking INTO the dark on PURPOSE?!

cards.question: The people who walk in the ways of darkness feel guilty every time they do evil.
The people who leave the straight paths walk paths that are ___ and ways that are devious.

cards.text: This rescue list is getting longer than the old receipts I used to sleep under in that junk drawer. It will also rescue the son from the forbidden woman, the stranger with seductive words, who has walked away from the partner of her youth.

cards.question: Besides walking away from the partner of her youth, what does the forbidden woman forget?

answers.text: The way back to her city

cards.text: Then the father gets very serious about where her house leads. No jokes on this card, friend. Lean in.

cards.question: Where does the forbidden woman's house sink?
People who go to the forbidden woman can come back and find the paths of life again.

cards.text: So where does all this guarding leave the son? On the right road, friend, with a GPS that NEVER has to say "recalculating."

cards.question: With wisdom guarding him, the son will follow in the ways of the ___ and keep to the paths of the righteous.

cards.text: The father closes with two groups of people and two VERY different endings. Friend, this is the part of the movie where I'm yelling at the screen, "PICK THE RIGHT DOOR!"

cards.question: What happens to the upright and the blameless?

answers.text: They inhabit the land and remain in it
They leave the land for a far country
They rule over the land as kings

cards.question: The wicked and the unfaithful will remain in the land alongside the upright.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says the father 'opens with one little word: IF.' Proverbs 2:1 actually opens with 'My son,' so the point he makes about the opening isn't true.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match.

findings.problem: Proverbs 2:5 promises two things: 'discern the fear of the LORD' and 'discover the knowledge of God.' The fear of the LORD is a key idea in Proverbs, and no story card or choice card in the walkthrough mentions it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences ('Now here's the twist.' / 'The son does all that digging…' / 'He just brings the shovel.'). It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to guess a word in the line, 'shield,' over 'teacher' or 'witness.' Card 10 only says 'one more title on His business card,' so nothing points to shield. In a passage about wisdom, 'teacher' is just as reasonable a pick, so getting it right comes down to luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The joke depends on the baker noticing 'the same four words he used back in verse 5' ('then you will discern'). No earlier card showed that wording. Card 7 only gave 'discover … the knowledge of God,' so the setup for the callback never came.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the exact list in 2:9 ('righteousness and justice and equity') against 'mercy and justice and peace' and 'strength and justice and honor.' Card 13 gives nothing to reason from, so the baker is guessing the line's wording. This is the same kind of question as the bad Psalm 23 oil example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'No jokes on this card, friend' talks about the app's cards. That points the baker at the app itself.

rule.text: What he never talks about: the app itself, its database, its files, or how lessons are made. Bakers never hear about any of that.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences ('Then the father gets very serious…' / 'No jokes on this card, friend.' / 'Lean in.'). It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Some cards weave exact BSB phrases into Papa Dorin's sentences without quotation marks. 'He adds hide my commandments within you' reads as broken grammar. Stop 1 card 13 does the same with 'Then you will discern, he says,' and so does stop 2 card 1 with 'the man who speaks perversity.' The docs say what quotation marks mean, but not whether exact Bible wording used inside a story card has to be quoted.
findings.question: When a story card uses exact BSB wording, must it be in quotation marks? Or is unquoted exact wording allowed as long as the sentence still reads naturally?
